I am 64 years old, been farming these 19 mu since I was 19. My father taught me, and now I manage it alone since my wife passed. Nineteen mu is a lot for one person, so I hire the machine team for plowing, sowing, and harvest — I pay them by the mu. I do the spraying, fertilizing, and irrigation myself because that saves money and I know my own fields.

For wheat, I plant Jimai 22, an improved variety. Last year I put 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at plowing time, then spread 25 kg of urea at jointing stage, and another 10 kg at heading when the ears were filling. That gave me around 480 kg per mu. This year I will do the same — I am not changing something that works. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't dry out, once at jointing when it shoots up fast, and once at heading for the grain filling. I spray herbicide right after sowing, and once more during the season if I see aphids or rust.

For maize, I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. I sow it immediately after wheat harvest in early June — I only have about 10 days, so I use no-till direct seeding. The machine plants right into the wheat stubble. I put 50 kg of compound fertilizer in the row at sowing, then 30 kg of urea at big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice: once when it is knee-high if the rain is poor, and once at filling stage. Maize gets three sprays: herbicide at sowing, then insecticide for corn borers twice because those pests come every summer and if you skip it they hollow out the stalks.

I use rotary tillage for wheat because maize stubble is thick and needs to be chopped and mixed into the soil. For maize, no-tillage — there is no time, and the wheat stubble actually helps keep moisture.

Some young people say I use too much fertilizer, but I have seen what happens when you cut back. In 2019 I tried reducing urea by half a bag per mu on 5 mu of maize and lost almost 100 kg per mu. That extra bag of urea costs maybe 60 yuan. Losing 100 kg of grain costs over 200 yuan. It is not a hard choice. I watch my neighbors too — the ones who do well use about the same as me. If everyone around you applies a certain amount, you do not go lower.
